<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sharingModel (symbol, 48 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **41** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `23ecff95c6968b314442eda7324049bf519d02cb` — the merge of head `e8f05ea1e59acccdea833b09fcdac22fa3225949` into base `609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 23ecff95c6968b314442eda7324049bf519d02cb && git checkout 23ecff95c6968b314442eda7324049bf519d02cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad e8f05ea1e59acccdea833b09fcdac22fa3225949 && git checkout -B drift-repro 609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad && git merge --no-ff e8f05ea1e59acccdea833b09fcdac22fa3225949

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 609b675135f1ea427aff463c551619a83368bcad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：管理员在员工离职、把工作交接给别人时，工时、报销明细、投票这类跟着上级记录走的明细记录，“所有人”不再被改成接手的人，仍然显示原来做事的人。明细里的审批人、负责人这类字段照旧交接。
- 为什么做：交接后，接手的人看起来像是录了离职者的工时、花了离职者的钱，审批和报表都会出错。这是你定为 p1 的临时修复，完整的按对象开关在另一张卡上。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是某些明细记录的所有人没有交接，管理员可以手动改，或交接它的上级记录。撤回即可。
- 要你做什么：无。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `3ae0a436fd` · 2026-11-19T09:57Z
- **Shape:** 4 files, +139/−2: `core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts` (+32), its existing test file (+85), the administrator guide (+8) and a changeset. Not governed. K = 12 since base `0967cbe6`, and it merges cleanly into current main.
- **Fixes vs card (#35344, the p1 interim bullet "until the switch exists, `controlled_by_parent` details should at least not be in the hand-over"):**
  - `userAssignedWorkFields` skips `owner_id` (`SystemFieldName.OWNER_ID`) when the object's `sharingModel` is `controlled_by_parent`.
  - The reading is flat ?? nested `security.sharingModel`, the same reading the access gates use (`masterGovernsRowWrites` and `effectiveSharingModel`). It is spelled once in this module because those packages depend on core. That is declared in the PR, and it is the right direction.
  - The detail's other user fields (approver, assignee) and `owner_id` on every other sharing model still count and move. Both the count and the transfer route read this one roster, so both narrow together.
  - The switch-following half (`userActions.transfer`, author-overridable) is #35399, `Blocked-by: #35315`. That matches the card's Order line.
- **Shipped shape: left out, not counted. Accepted for the interim.**
  - The card's "the panel can still count those records" belongs to the switch design. The only reason the count answer can carry today is `transferable: false`, and the panel words that as "lists several people", which is false for an owner column. A true sentence needs new keys in seven locale catalogues.
  - Folding the counted shape into #35399 is the right home. That is the seat's question, and I agree with the dev's recommendation.
- **Pins:** 6 new cases in the existing `user-assigned-work.test.ts`, with a twin control. The ablation (deleting the skip line) turns 5 of the 6 red while the control stays green. The dogfood battery is green (4092 passed).
- **Changeset and level (asked): `patch` with a BREAKING banner is correct.**
  - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right. The published `assigned-work` GET and `transfer` POST answers and core's exported `userAssignedWorkFields` roster all drop a row they used to carry, which is BREAKING.
  - `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no authorable key or value is added, refused or re-meant. `sharingModel: controlled_by_parent` still means "access follows the master", and the hand-over now derives from that. The L2 should confirm this against `semantic`.
  - AGENTS.md: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". All three are present. The disposition is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which fits because nothing an author writes is removed or renamed and nothing stored is rewritten.
  - I read it sentence by sentence: the narrowed endpoints, the BREAKING audience, the "Unchanged" paragraph and the remedy (hand over the master) all match the code and the guide.
- **Gates:** CI on `3ae0a436` is 61 success and 12 skipped, with 0 failed. "Check Changeset" (which runs the ADR-0087 registration check) was still running at review time and must be green before queueing.
- **L2 owed:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, so the seat writes a CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 over the whole non-prose diff. The face is the roster's narrowing, plus the counted-shape question for #35399.
- **Landing clause:** not governed, so ux-1 lands it after the seat's L2 record. K < 15, so no main merge is required. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3ae0a436fdaeee93aeb765cc5a94949965ed0edc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts, packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/system-names.ts, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md, packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/UserAssignedWorkPanel.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **What was read.** Card #35344 with its three comments, the PR body and its three comments (the L1 ACCEPT 7005782432 among them), the net diff against `main` (4 files, +139/−2), the 74 check-runs on this head, and two things the hunks and the claim cite, read only to check the citation: the ruling comment 7000907189 on #35315, and the title, state and body of #35399. The cited files on the `Scope:` line were read on `main`, none reviewed.
- **Core export `userAssignedWorkFields`: narrowed, named right.** The roster drops the pair (detail object, `owner_id`) when the object's `sharingModel` is `controlled_by_parent`. No exported type moves: `ObjectLike` is module-private and `UserAssignedWorkField` is unchanged.
- **`GET .../assigned-work`: narrowed, named right.** The pair leaves `objects[]`, and its count leaves `total`.
- **`POST .../assigned-work/transfer`: narrowed, named right.** The detail's owner is never read or written, it is not part of `remaining`, and a call whose `objects` names the detail alone moves the detail's other user fields only. The request is still accepted with 200: no accept set moves and no refusal is added.
- **One roster, two readers.** `countUserAssignedWork` and `transferUserAssignedWork` are the only callers of the roster, and `packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.ts` is the only caller of those two. Count and transfer narrow together; no door is left on the old roster.
- **Nothing widens.** No accept set, no key, no value, no route, no export is added. The value half of the declaration therefore overstates (N1).
- **The predicate reads what the gates read.** `accessFollowsMaster` is `sharingModel ?? security?.sharingModel === 'controlled_by_parent'`, the same expression as `masterGovernsRowWrites` (plugin-security) and the `controlled_by_parent` arm of `effectiveSharingModel` (plugin-sharing). The docblock's two reasons for spelling it in core hold: both plugins depend on `@objectstack/core`, and `@objectstack/spec` exports no object-level reader (`controlledByParentMasterRefusal` takes the model as an argument, `controlledByParentMasterOf` takes the field map).
- **Spec untouched.** No path under `packages/spec` is in the diff, so no authorable-surface or authorable-defaults baseline moves.
- **Panel untouched, and its wording stays true.** The panel prints `console.assignedWork.notTransferable` ("Lists several people, so it cannot be handed over here.") under every row the server answers `transferable: false`. A left-out row is not in the answer, so the panel renders nothing for it and never says a detail's owner lists several people. `splitAssignedWork`'s owned total shrinks by the same rows.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on `@objectstack/core` is right.** Core is the only released package the diff moves. The level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` line alone, and `none` takes `patch`; the breaking-ness rides the `!`, the `**BREAKING**` banner and the `(narrowing)` arm, all three present.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` holds against `semantic`.** `semantic` is "the meaning or default of an authorable key changes". The spec's statement of `controlled_by_parent` on `main` ("access is derived from the master record") is unchanged and stays true, no default moves, and the same stored metadata parses to the same object. What moved is one platform feature's roster rule, which now reads that existing declaration. The one stock `semantic` changeset on `main` (`required` beside its own `visibleWhen`) changed what the authored key itself enforces on a write; this diff changes nothing the key enforces. The protocol change proper is the object-level switch (`userActions.transfer`), which arrives as `added` with #35315 and #35399.
- **ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, and the right category.** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` fits: nothing an author writes is removed, renamed or refused, nothing stored is rewritten, no exported declaration changes (so none of the symbol-naming categories applies), and there is nothing to register a conversion for. The category is refused only beside `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, which is not declared and would be wrong here. `Check Changeset` (both runs) and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head.
- **Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and they agree.** The `Skills-docs:` line the arm owes is present, and its claim holds: no file under `skills/` names the assigned-work routes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Shape shipped (dev flag, and open question 1): settled by the seat.** The left-out shape ships now. The counted-but-not-moved shape folds into #35399, which is open and `Blocked-by: #35315`. Recorded as settled; this record does not reopen it. The reason given is true on `main`: the only reason the count answer can carry is `transferable: false`, and the panel words it as a multi-valued field.
- **Predicate spelled in core (dev flag): accepted.** See ①. The dev's observation that plugin-security, plugin-sharing, objectql and now core each spell the reading is correct and reproduces no wrong answer; it stays an acceptance note.
- **Optional-master corner (dev flag): not answered on the shipped faces.** The PR body states it; the docblock, the guide and the changeset state the opposite. This is S1.
- **Open question 2 (the form of the maintainer brief in the PR body): the seat's.** It is not a contract question and has no bearing on the narrowing. `PR-body guards` is `success` on this head.
- **Dogfood battery owed by the `(narrowing)` arm and the `!` title: present and pinned to this head.** The os-dev-report on the card (comment 7005706977) carries `dogfood_battery` opening with `3ae0a436fd`, the full command with no shard and no path, lock verdict exit 0, 482 files and 4092 tests passed, no failure. The PR-run `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` with its shard job skipped, as PR runs are; the queue adds the shards.
- **Check-runs on this head:** 74 runs, 62 `success`, 12 `skipped`, none failed or pending. Every required context is `success` except `Lint UI`, skipped with no `ui/` diff.
- **SQL push-down: nothing to find.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. It removes one (object, field) pair from an in-memory roster built from the registry, so the detail's owner gets no `count` and no `find` at all. The pre-existing per-row transfer loop is untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real?** Neither exactly. The spec refuses nothing here, and the hand-over of a detail's owner was a delivered behaviour, not a declared-and-undelivered one. It is withdrawn on a maintainer ruling: the derived default for owner transfer is off on a `controlled_by_parent` detail (point 1 of comment 7000907189), the offboarding hand-over follows that switch (point 5), and the card's own interim bullet asks for exactly this until the switch exists. The raw write is left alone, as point 2 of the same ruling requires: `owner_id` stays `readonly: false`, so a by-hand owner edit still works. The withdrawal is at the right layer, the one roster both doors read, and it is keyed on the declaration the access gates key on. The half the ruling also grants, "authors override both ways", does not exist in the interim; #35399 carries it.

Attempts to break it, and what held:
- A transfer naming the detail alone cannot reach the owner: `objects` filters the already-narrowed roster.
- `remaining` cannot stall the caller's repeat-until-zero loop, because the left-out pair is not counted there either. A counted row added naively to `remaining` would have stalled it; the left-out shape avoids that.
- A detail of a detail is skipped on its own declaration; the top master's owner still moves.
- An object with no owner column (`ownership` other than `user`) has nothing to skip.
- With `sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit`, the leaver's dormant owner leg costs the successor nothing: handing over the master gives edit on the master, which admits every write of the detail.
- The five pins that depend on the skip line and the twin control that does not are consistent with the ablation the dev reports.

What did not hold:

No must-fix.

**S1 (should-fix) — the narrowing's stated premise is false for one row class ADR-0055 declares, and that class is stranded with no notice on any shipped face.**
- The docblock says "A detail's access follows its master (ADR-0055), so its owner is not who holds the work". ADR-0055 as amended for the optional master says otherwise for a row whose master reference is empty: it is read by its owner and by View All on the detail, and written by its owner and by Modify All. The spec's own `sharingModel` jsdoc repeats the read half. For those rows the owner is the only holder below an administrator. The ADR's example is a contact with no account.
- The skip is per object, so it covers them. Before this head a banned user's null-master rows were counted and moved. On this head they are not counted, not moved and not in `remaining`, the banned owner cannot sign in, and only View All reads them. In a chain, the details under such a row are read through it, so they go with it.
- The guide and the changeset give one remedy, "Hand over the master record". These rows have no master. Nothing in the count answer tells the administrator they exist.
- The PR body says this to the maintainer. The docblock, the administrator guide and the changeset, which ships as the package's CHANGELOG, do not; they say the opposite.
- The behaviour matches the ruled object-level default, so the smallest fix is on the prose faces. The guide and the changeset name the row class (a detail row that names no master, on an optional master), what happens to it, and the remedy that exists: a holder of Modify All on the detail filters the detail by owner and edits the owner by hand. #35399 gains the corner as a line, since the dev report names it as the carrier and its body does not have it.
- The alternative is the seat's or the maintainer's to choose, not this record's: keep the owner pair for an optional-master detail, restricted to rows whose master reference is empty, as one pushed-down `IS NULL` conjunct in the same `count` and `find`. That is finer than the ruled object-level default.

Nits, none of which changes a verdict above:
- **N1 (nit, prose face) — the declaration reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; the diff widens nothing, so the exact spelling is `no (narrowing)`.** The one reader defines `yes (narrowing)` as a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. No gate decides differently on it: the level follows the kind, and the breaking-ness and this review's face follow the arm. The spelling came from the claim. Left as it stands it is an accepted deviation; correct it in the PR body and the changeset together if the changeset moves for S1.
- **N2 (nit, follow-up) — two published jsdoc summaries are now wider than the answer.** `security.assignedWork.count` in `packages/client/src/index.ts` and `registerUserWorkEndpoints` in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` both say "the owner field and every app user field". Neither file is in the diff, and touching either moves a second package. #35399 rewrites the count answer and should rewrite both sentences with it.
- **N3 (nit, follow-up) — #35399 does not yet carry the wording constraint its counted shape depends on.** Its body says the panel still counts those records. It should also say that a counted detail-owner row needs its own reason sentence and must never reuse `notTransferable`. The key lives in eleven locale catalogues on `main`, not seven.
- **N4 (nit) — no pin states the optional-master behaviour.** Every new fixture declares its master `required: true`. Once S1 is decided, one case with `required: false` and a null-master row makes the outcome a decision the suite holds. It belongs with #35399 unless the code moves for S1.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35344-handover-skip-detail-owner`
Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35428`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a, delta) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `e8f05ea1e5` (reviewed delta `3ae0a436fd..26ff98c888`) · 2026-11-19T10:54Z
- **Delta reviewed:** 3 files, +38/−20, prose only: the `user-assigned-work.ts` docblock, `administrator-guide.mdx` and the changeset. No code line changes. My round-1 ACCEPT was 7005782432. The round answers the seat's L2 7006025069 (S1 and N1).
  - `e8f05ea1` merges main only: I checked that the PR's own diff against main's parent is identical before and after the merge.
- **S1 is closed in prose, consistently on all three surfaces.** A detail row that names its master is reached through it, so handing the master over hands its access. The added row class is a null-master row on an optional master (`required: false`, ADR-0055 as amended):
  - its owner reads and writes it beside View All / Modify All;
  - its owner is also left out, because the skip is per object;
  - after a ban only View All / Modify All holders reach it;
  - the remedy is a Modify All holder filtering by owner and editing it by hand.

  That matches the code, which skips `owner_id` per object regardless of the row's master value. The ADR-0055 citation moved from "access follows the master" in general to the row-that-names-a-master case, which is more precise.
- **N1:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` now matches `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:113-116`, since the diff widens nothing. The BREAKING banner, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the ADR-0087 marker and the patch level are unchanged.
- **Changeset (re-read sentence by sentence):** the reworded BREAKING paragraph, the "Unchanged" paragraph and the new null-master paragraph all match the code and the guide.
